REASONING:  
From EQ1 we have for all elements \(x,y\)  

\[
x = (y*y)*(x*x).
\]

Define the unary map \(f(t)=t*t\).  Then EQ1 rewrites as  

\[
x = f(y)*f(x) \qquad(\forall x,y). \tag{1}
\]

**Step 1 – Left‑argument irrelevance.**  
Fix any \(a,b\in\operatorname{Im}(f)\).  Choose \(y\) with \(f(y)=a\) and \(x\) with \(f(x)=b\).  Substituting these into (1) gives  

\[
x = a * b .
\]

Thus for every pair \((a,b)\) with \(a,b\) in the image of \(f\) the product \(a*b\) is *independent of the left argument* and equals the unique element \(x\) satisfying \(f(x)=b\).  Consequently there is a function \(g:\operatorname{Im}(f)\to S\) (where \(S\) is the underlying set) such that  

\[
a*b = g(b)\qquad(\forall a,b\in\operatorname{Im}(f)). \tag{2}
\]

**Step 2 – \(f\) is an involution.**  
From (1) with \(y\) arbitrary and \(x\) such that \(f(x)=b\) we obtain  

\[
g(b)=x\quad\text{and}\quad f(x)=b .
\]

Hence \(g\) is the inverse of \(f\) on \(\operatorname{Im}(f)\); in particular \(f\) is bijective on its image and  

\[
f(f(t))=t\qquad(\forall t\in S). \tag{3}
\]

Thus \(f\) is an involution.

**Step 3 – General form of the operation.**  
Equations (2) and (3) together give the complete description of any magma satisfying EQ1:

\[
a*b = f(b)\qquad(\forall a,b\in S),\tag{4}
\]

where \(f\) is a unary involution (\(f\circ f =\operatorname{id}\)).  (For left arguments not in \(\operatorname{Im}(f)\) the value is forced by (4) as well, because \(\operatorname{Im}(f)=S\) by (3).)

**Step 4 – Deriving EQ2.**  
Using (4) we compute the right‑hand side of EQ2:

\[
\begin{aligned}
y *\bigl((x * (z * y)) * x\bigr)
&= f\!\bigl((x * (z * y)) * x\bigr) \\
&= f\!\bigl(f\bigl(f(y)\bigr) * x\bigr) \qquad(\text{since }z*y = f(y),\; x*(z*y)=f(f(y))=y)\\
&= f\!\bigl(f(x)\bigr) \\
&= x \qquad\text{by (3).}
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the right‑hand side of EQ2 reduces to \(x\) for every assignment, i.e.  

\[
x = y * ((x * (z * y)) * x)
\]

holds in every magma that satisfies EQ1.

Since every model of EQ1 also satisfies EQ2, the implication “EQ1 ⇒ EQ2” is valid over all magmas.

PROOF: The derivation above shows that any magma satisfying EQ1 must be of the form \(a*b = f(b)\) with \(f\) an involution, and for such a magma EQ2 reduces to the identity \(x=x\). Hence EQ2 follows from EQ1.
